subject.title: config: use datetime suffix for config backup files instead of numeric rotation

question: Should timestamped config backups preserve or convert existing numbered `.bak.N` recovery points, or may the migration delete them when the suffix scheme changes?
rationale: Config backups are recovery and sensitive-data artifacts, so first-write deletion of shipped backup slots is an upgrade behavior decision rather than a mechanical cleanup choice.

options.title: Require upgrade-safe migration
options.body: Keep the PR open but require preserving or converting legacy `.bak.N` files until retention is safely replenished, with focused tests and real upgrade proof.

options.title: Accept first-write pruning
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally allow deleting legacy numbered backups, but the PR should document that upgrade behavior and prove the remaining recovery path is acceptable.

options.title: Pause for broader layout design
options.body: Pause this naming-only PR if the dedicated backup-directory request should own the permanent backup layout and migration path.

recommendation.title: Require upgrade-safe migration
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open but require preserving or converting legacy `.bak.N` files until retention is safely replenished, with focused tests and real upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history and review context around config backup and recovery behavior.
